TODAY
Warm near-black + gold, Fraunces serif with an italic gold accent phrase, uppercase letterspaced gold eyebrow, gold-fill button.

All five of those appear in the Tiger Boards email. Fraunces is also one of the most widely used free display serifs on the web — part of why you keep seeing it.

A · INSTRUMENT — my recommendation
Cool near-black (not warm), no serif at all, Archivo display + IBM Plex Sans/Mono. Tabular mono numerals and tick rules carry the emphasis instead of a decorative italic. Mint-cyan signal used small, semantic amber/red reserved for real status.

Why: reads as measurement, not marketing. Deliverable via your token system — no component rebuild.
Tradeoff: colder. Undersells the senior-practitioner story a CFO buyer may respond to.

B · DOCUMENT
Inverts to light-dominant paper — the single fastest way to stop resembling every dark-gold competitor. Newsreader serif, oxblood ink, clause numbering, marginalia, a real SoA extract. No gold anywhere.

Why: signals rigour and permanence; looks like the auditor's actual world.
Tradeoff: risks reading as a law firm or standards body — trading one costume for another — and least obviously software.

C · CONSOLE
The marketing page IS the product surface. Neutral app canvas, your existing Manrope + JetBrains Mono, and the status palette (pass/warn/gap) becomes the brand palette.

Why: the most defensible differentiation — derived from an asset only you own. A newsletter cannot fake a control register.
Tradeoff: the most work, needs real component fidelity, and de-emphasises the human consulting story that currently closes deals.
